title: Ten years of teaching machines to feel
thesis: In 2016, AI that understands emotion in video sounded like science fiction. Ten years on, mood is a standard line on every metadata spec sheet. The interesting part is what Vionlabs got wrong on the way, and what Arash would tell a founder starting in media AI today.
whyNow: The point of Arash's LinkedIn system is to make him a recognised voice in AI and streaming, and personal build stories travel further than product posts. 2026 is ten years since Vionlabs was founded, and the market has just caught up with the original bet: in the radar's first edition, five competitors were selling mood metadata.
questions: What was the original bet in 2016, and who thought it was crazy?
What did we build early that nobody wanted?
Which change of direction mattered most, and how did we know?
What is different about selling to broadcasters, streamers and telcos?
What would Arash tell a founder starting a media-AI company in 2026?
bring: Arash's own story in his words, the team that built it, early photos and the first pitch deck. Nothing here can be researched: it comes from voice notes.
needs: Three voice notes from Arash, 5–10 minutes each (the pack gives the prompts)
Old photos and a slide or two from the first pitch deck
Teammates and early partners to credit by name, with their OK
events: IAMT London Conference & Awards (1–2 Dec) as a natural moment for the closing post
radar: 2026-W43 theme: Metadata enrichment is what personalisation runs on (the market caught up)
